firmware.title: v3.96 (~450 Hz, 2 real measurements per loop, shorter power phase)
firmware.summary: v3.62 on a faster scan loop. Wacom charges the pen with 13 transmit bursts (1.64 ms) every loop; the pen works the same with 9 (tested: pressure, buttons, hover like stock; 8 is too few), so the loop takes 4.47 ms instead of 4.97 ms: ~224 loops/s instead of ~201. The carrier stays unbroken (any pause in it confuses the pen). Everything else is v3.62: two real position measurements per loop (S1 and the pen-data scan S2 listening on the neighbour coils), Wacom's own calculation with a constant 4-result average, exactly one report per measurement (~448/s), no interpolation or prediction; short hover signal dips passed on as in range for up to 150 ms.
firmware.short: Method: two measurements. The pen-data part of each scan also locates the pen, so it is measured twice per scan, and the pen-charging part is shorter than Wacom's, so there are ~224 scans/s instead of ~201: ~448 real reports/s, exactly one per measurement, nothing added in between.

firmware.title: v3.85 (~750 Hz, two measurements)
firmware.summary: v2.45 with the second real measurement per scan loop: while the pen sends its pressure and button data, the neighbouring wires listen too, so the pen is located twice per loop (~400 times/s instead of ~200). The second position is used only when its signal is strong and matches the first (never at the top / left edge). Everything else is v2.45: Wacom's calculation runs 4 times per loop, Wacom's own reports (~750/s, one per USB poll), Wacom's own smoothing for drawing and hover, stock pressure, buttons and hover. No extra output code or diagnostics.
firmware.short: Method: two measurements + more Wacom runs. The pen is measured twice per scan (~400 times/s), and Wacom's own calculation turns that into ~750 smooth reports/s, like v2.45. Straighter lines and a calmer cursor than v2.45 in tests.

firmware.title: v2.45 (recommended)
firmware.summary: Recommended. Stock pen scanning (the pen is measured ~206 times/s) with one change: Wacom's calc also runs on the set-1 pass-a frame when the coil window is unchanged, so every measurement loop gives 4 reports instead of 3 (~730 reports/s). The extra reports are Wacom's smoothed in-between positions. Stock pressure, side buttons, hover and filters.
firmware.short: Method: more Wacom runs. Same ~200 measurements/s as stock, Wacom's calculation runs 4 times per measurement: 4 small cursor steps instead of 1 big one (~730 reports/s). Smooth, calm hover, the most tested.

firmware.title: v3.78 (~1500 Hz, 2 real measurements per loop)
firmware.summary: Two real measurements per scan loop as v3.62 (S1 position scan + S2 pen-data scan listening on the neighbour coils, normalised per burst; S2 only with a strong signal and a matching coil, stock S2 at the top / left edge). Wacom's calc gets up to 7 frames per loop (steps 23-29; step 23 only when the coil window is unchanged, 25-27 are transmit-only steps with complete data) and averages a constant 7 results (~1 loop), so ~1500 results/s, each a real Wacom output, sent two per USB packet. Top / left strip (Wacom extrapolates there): extra smoothing when the pen is slow or still, none when fast. USB packets wait in a small queue until the PC collects the previous one, so none are dropped, and extra-frame results stay valid after the pen re-enters range.
firmware.short: Method: two measurements, like v3.62 (~400 measurements/s), plus more Wacom runs: its calculation runs ~7 times per scan, ~1500 reports/s sent two per USB packet. Calmer top / left edges. Newest and least tested.

firmware.title: v3.28 (2000 Hz, even)
firmware.summary: ~1900-2000 reports/s: two reports every 1 ms, sent together in one USB packet (the PC splits them). Stock pen scanning and Wacom's own processing exactly as v2.45 (stock pressure, side buttons, hover, filters), with a new output stage written in C that sends evenly spaced reports on the path of Wacom's own positions. No prediction: every report lies between two positions Wacom has already delivered (a fixed delay keeps them available), so there is no overshoot. The four positions of each ~4.85 ms scan loop are placed evenly in time, so the cursor moves at a steady speed within the loop. Extra smoothing only where Wacom's output is rough: the top/left edge strip at slow speed and a spike filter at the limit of hover height. The price of the even timing is ~2 ms more lag than v2.45.
firmware.short: Method: even output. Same as v3.29 with two reports every 1 ms (2000/s), sent together in one USB packet.

firmware.title: v3.29 (1000 Hz, even)
firmware.summary: 1000 reports/s, one every 1 ms. Stock pen scanning and Wacom's own processing exactly as v2.45 (stock pressure, side buttons, hover, filters), with a new output stage written in C that sends evenly spaced reports on the path of Wacom's own positions. No prediction: every report lies between two positions Wacom has already delivered (a fixed delay keeps them available), so there is no overshoot. The four positions of each ~4.85 ms scan loop are placed evenly in time, so the cursor moves at a steady speed within the loop. Extra smoothing only where Wacom's output is rough: the top/left edge strip at slow speed and a spike filter at the limit of hover height. The price of the even timing is ~2 ms more lag than v2.45.
firmware.short: Method: even output. v2.45's measurements, reports placed exactly every 1 ms (1000/s) on the path between measured positions, no prediction.

firmware.title: v2.99 (1000 Hz, interpolated)
firmware.summary: Stock pen scanning (~206 real positions/s, same as stock) with a new output stage: exactly one report per 1 ms USB tick (1000 evenly spaced reports/s instead of v2.45's bunched ~730). Each report lies on the straight line between the two newest real measurements (Wacom's per-scan position, without its 4-report smoothing); no prediction, never beyond the newest real point. Stock pressure, side buttons and hover. Slightly more lag than v2.45: the 6 ms fill delay is what keeps every report between two real measurements.
firmware.short: Older build, replaced by v3.29. Method: even output. v2.45's measurements, one report exactly every 1 ms (1000/s) on the path between measured positions, no prediction.

firmware.title: v1.65 (600 Hz)
firmware.summary: Stock pen scanning; Wacom's calc also runs after both S2 passes, so every measurement loop gives 3 reports (~600 reports/s) instead of 1. The extra reports are Wacom's smoothed in-between positions. Stable fallback, but in fast drags every 4th report is missing (fixed in v2.45).
firmware.short: Older build, replaced by v2.45. Method: more Wacom runs. Same ~200 measurements/s as stock, Wacom's calculation runs 3 times per measurement (~600 reports/s).

firmware.title: Wacom stock v1.51 / v1.52
firmware.summary: Original Wacom firmware. Measures the pen ~206 times/s and sends one report per measurement (~200 reports/s). Wacom's 4-report smoothing then spans ~4 measurements, which makes it the laggiest option. Use it to restore the tablet to factory firmware.
firmware.short: The original Wacom firmware. The pen is measured ~200 times per second and each measurement gives one report (~200 reports/s).
